comment.body:
## Real flood semantics (rd mallcoppro-8ac9, ruled by Baron 2026-07-15)

**Do not merge without human review** — this remains a GATED self-authored detector.

### The bug

`authored-deploy-flood` fired severity:high on **every single** `github.deployment` event — no counting, no window, no baseline. Despite the name and docs ("a flood of deployments"), it was a false-positive cannon: any normal deploy on any customer repo would have escalated. The old benign-twin only proved a *different event type* (`github.push`) stays silent — it never proved a single legitimate deployment stays silent, which it did not.

### The fix

`Detect` (`core/detect/authored/deployflood/deployflood.go`) now counts `github.deployment` events per actor across the given event set and compares the count against that actor's baseline deployment frequency via `pkg/baseline.Baseline.FreqCountActor("github", "github.deployment", actor)` — the same 3-segment `source:event_type:actor` key shape the corpus `frequency_tables` and the framework's `volume-anomaly` detector both use (mirrored, not invented).

It fires only on a genuine burst:
- `count >= 8` (absolute floor) **regardless of baseline** — a flood with no history still fires, or
- `count > 3 × baseline` once the baseline is established (`>= 3`, so a thin baseline can't be gamed into a "3×" false alarm off noise).

A single deployment, or a volume the baseline already explains, never fires. Severity stays `high`, but only for a real flood. Stays pure (no I/O, no package-state mutation, read-only over `events`/`bl`) — passes the K7 shape gate and the K2a import allow-list unchanged.

### Scenarios rewritten

- **must-fire**: 10 `github.deployment` events from one actor (`burst-actor`) against a zero baseline — a genuine burst.
- **benign-twin**: **one** `github.deployment` event from an actor with an established baseline (5) — this is the key fix: the benign is now a real deployment, not a different event type, so the gate actually tests flood-vs-single.

`chain_action` stays past-tense (`escalated`/`resolved`) per the corpus convention (already fixed on this branch).

`exams/scenarios/corpus.pin` regenerated via the loader's own `scanCorpus`/`Manifest` mechanism — count unchanged at 60 (same two scenarios, changed content), so no downstream composition constants needed touching (verified: merge-gate 41/19 split, `guard_test.go`'s count-60 anchors, `harness_test.go`'s `wantAttacks`/`wantBenigns` all still hold as-is, unmodified).

### Sabotage check (required by the task)

Added `core/detect/authored/deployflood/deployflood_test.go`:
- A single event lifted out of the must-fire burst does **not** fire the new detector — proves the must-fire verdict genuinely requires volume, not mere presence of a `github.deployment` event.
- The reconstructed **old** naive logic (fire on any `github.deployment` event) **would** have fired on that same single event, and on the benign-twin's single deployment — reproducing the exact bug this fixes.

### Verification

`core/eval`'s own in-process tests never link the authored-detector aggregator (by design — they stay a detector-agnostic reference-corpus grader); the real gate is the built product binary. Built `cmd/mallcop` (which does blank-import `core/detect/authored`) and ran the real `mallcop exam-detect`:

- `authored-deploy-flood-must-fire`: **PASS** (fires, as expected)
- `authored-deploy-flood-benign-twin`: **PASS** (silent, as expected)
- 9 pre-existing RED rows elsewhere in the corpus are unrelated detection gaps, unchanged by this commit (tracked as targets, not introduced here).

`go test ./...`: green, all packages, 0 failures (`core/selfgate` ~86s).
`TestHarness_MergeGate_GreenWithMedianOfN`: **PASS** — median pass rate 1.0000 (60/60), recall 1.0 (41/41), precision 1.0 (19/19).

Branch: one commit on top of the existing vocabulary-fix commit, rebased onto current `main`, pushed with `--force-with-lease`.

comment.body:
## Live-proof result (mallcop-e2e branch `work/selfext-egress-b-proof`, run 29421569762)

Dispatched one `workflow_dispatch` against a branch of `mallcop-app/mallcop-e2e`
pinned to this branch head (`d3f7c10`). Rail `donut-byoi`, budget $2, detector
`authored-deploy-burst` / `github.deployment`. **Result: author job failed at the
egress-jail proof — but far past where the container version died, and $0 spend
(authoring never ran).**

### What this PR proved works (all green on a bare GitHub-hosted runner)
- Toolchain reproduction pre-jail: opencode `@1.17.11` (pinned, `--ignore-scripts`),
  Go 1.25 (setup-go), Node 24 (setup-node), `mallcop-ops` + `mallcop` from
  **SHA-256-verified** release tarballs (`sha256sum -c` passed), bundled config.
- `--exam-repo` reference tree checkout: `mallcop-app/mallcop@v0.9.3` → `_exam` (green).
- Opener-scripts checkout via `github.job_workflow_sha` → `_selfext` (green).
- `go mod download` pre-fetch (green).
- harden-runner planted (green). **The fail-closed egress proof then correctly
  refused to author under an unproven jail — the gate works as designed.**

Contrast with the container run `29314104398`, which died at step 6 (egress proof)
because harden-runner cannot enforce egress inside a container. RULING B's container
removal is validated: we now get all the way to the jail-proof step.

### Two blockers discovered (both require a design/infra decision — NOT code bugs)

**A. `mallcop-e2e` is a PRIVATE repo → harden-runner block mode is a paid-tier
feature for private repos.** The pre-step config logged `"private":true`,
`"api_key":""`; the agent initialized in **audit** mode (`NewAuditClient created`,
`added audit rules`) despite `egress_policy:block`, enforcing only the global
malicious-IP blocklist. The planted `curl https://example.com` was logged but **not
blocked** → fail-closed proof (correctly) failed. Ref: StepSecurity docs — "Private
repository support ... is part of the platform's paid tier."

**B. harden-runner enforces from the job-start pre-hook, not from its step
position.** Per StepSecurity: it "installs eBPF hooks at the kernel level before any
user-defined workflow steps execute." So placing the pinned toolchain downloads
*before* the harden-runner step does NOT run them outside the jail. Under **real**
block enforcement (public repo / paid tier) the pre-jail download hosts (npm
registry, nodejs.org, Go dist, opencode release) — which RULING B said not to
allowlist — would be **blocked**, breaking the toolchain install. The "downloads
pre-jail, jail after via step ordering" model is not achievable with harden-runner.

### Recommendation (needs a ruling)
- **Enforcement:** either (i) enable a StepSecurity subscription for the org's
  private repos, or (ii) run the live proof on a public dogfood repo, or (iii) drop
  the harden-runner dependency and self-enforce egress (nftables default-deny) —
  which also resolves B.
- **For B specifically:** split into two jobs — an un-jailed `setup` job that
  reproduces + **caches** the toolchain and Go modules, and a `author` job with
  harden-runner as the true first step (jail from job start) that restores the cache
  and runs authoring under the minimal allowlist. This is the only way to keep the
  allowlist free of download hosts while the jail is up from job start.

This PR faithfully implements RULING B as written and is correct for audit-mode /
container-removal purposes; findings A and B mean a follow-up ruling is needed before
a green *block-enforced* proof is possible. **Do not merge without that decision.**

## Stale-PR refresh (rd mallcoppro-aa8)

Refreshed per Baron's 2026-07-15 refresh-then-review ruling. **Do not merge without human review** — this remains a GATED self-authored detector; this refresh only brings the branch current and fixes scenario-data typos so the eval gate can adjudicate the detector's real behavior.

### What changed

1. **Rebased onto current main** (`42a66ca`, 34 commits ahead of the old base). One conflict: `exams/scenarios/corpus.pin` — resolved by regenerating with the loader-derived throwaway `TestRegenPin` helper (the mechanism `corpus.pin`'s own header documents), not by hand-merging. `core/detect/authored/registry.go`'s append-only blank import applied cleanly.
2. **Guard proof-mutation fixtures refreshed** (`core/selfgate/guard_test.go` lines 352/802): the fixtures anchor on the literal pinned count via `replaceOnce`, which self-reports "the repo under test changed; update the proof mutation" — updated `count 58` anchors to `count 60`. ## Summary

Implements C8 (rd `mallcoppro-c78`) — corpus-expansion axis iii, the OPT-IN

- **Sandbox**: `sanitizeScenarioForContribution` deep-copies the local
  scenario (yaml round-trip, never touches the source file) and runs a
  deterministic two-pass sanitize:
  1. **Identity pass** — every distinct actor found anywhere in the document
     (events, finding metadata, actor_chain, baseline known_entities/
     actor_roles/actor_hours/relationships) is renamed to a canonical
     corpus-style token (`ci-bot`, `admin-user`, ... — first-seen order,
     20-token pool with a content-hash fallback), including a longest-first
     substring pass over prose fields so a name mentioned in free text
     doesn't survive.
  2. **Identifier pass** — residual UUIDs / emails / long all-hex runs
     (e.g. an Azure subscription id) get a deterministic `sub-<hash8>` /
     `id-<hash8>` token, matching VA-03's `sub-<hex8>` convention. Built as a
     single non-overlapping pass over the *original* string (not chained
     regex replacements) so an inserted hash token can never be re-matched
     and re-hashed by a later pass.
  - Secret-shaped metadata values are redacted by **reusing**
    `scrubPayloadMap` from `cli/scenariocapture.go` (C5 #190) — not forked.
  - Timestamps are shifted by one constant duration so every relative delta
    (fine event spacing *and* multi-month baseline relationship history) is
    preserved exactly, anchored so the earliest event lands on
    `2026-03-10T08:00:00Z` (VA-03's own start).
- **Gate**: `provenance: authored` scenarios are refused by default
  (author-independence — the commons should predominantly grow from
  operator/captured ground truth); `--allow-authored` overrides.
- **PR**: corpus.pin is regenerated against the manifest-relative `RelPath`

  then returns *before* any git/gh invocation is reachable. The PR body

## Review round 2 fixes (commit c4e03a3)

**[HIGH-1] Sanitizer-blind struct fields — FIXED.** Event `id:`, event `action:` (the promoted-payload case), `actor_chain[].action`, `connector_tools[].name`/`description`, and `tags[]` are all wired into both the actor-substring pass and the identifier scrub. Event ids get **shape-preserving span tokenization**: only identifier-shaped substrings are replaced (`azure-<uuid>-000123` → `azure-id-<hash8>-000123`), through the document-wide shared hash cache — ordering and uniqueness survive, and `finding.event_ids` receives the byte-identical transform so the cross-reference stays intact (asserted).

**[HIGH-2] frequency_tables actor segments — FIXED.** Keys get exact per-segment actor renames (position-independent — handles both `source:event_type:actor` and the extended `source:event_type:actor:N:period` per `pkg/baseline`'s ActorTypeCount construction; count values are never touched) plus the identifier scrub. Actors appearing **only** in freq keys (segment index 2) are now collected into the actor map, so an aged-out-but-baselined actor renames everywhere. The regression test proves a captured-with-baseline scenario — the primary feedstock — contributes successfully end-to-end through the real dry-run path, with renamed keys, preserved counts, and an `exam.Load` round-trip.

**[MED-1] Pool-token false abort — FIXED.** `buildContributeActorMap` now skips pool tokens that contain or are contained by any collected actor original (≥3 bytes, matching the gate's own skip); the hash fallback salts deterministically until conflict-free. An actor literally named `admin` no longer lands anyone on `admin-user`/`infra-admin`, so the gate's substring check stays sound. The gate's error message now names the tokenizer-collision cause for the theoretically-unreachable residual case instead of misdiagnosing it as a leak.

**[MED-2] Real-TLD blocklist collisions — FIXED.** `sh`, `md`, `rs`, `py`, and `zip` (all real TLDs) are removed from the filename-extension filter — `status.realcorp.sh` now tokenizes to `host-<hash8>.example` and appears in the ledger. Dotted filenames with those endings get hostname-tokenized instead: over-redaction bias, and the ledger shows the operator exactly what was replaced. Non-TLD extensions (`js`, `go`, `gz`, `db`, ...) stay filtered so ordinary filenames survive.

**Tests.** Three new regressions built from the reviewer's proven-leak shapes, all through the real `runScenarioContribute --dry-run` path: `AuxiliaryFieldLeaks_Scrubbed` (grep-class residue over both transmit artifacts + ledger enumeration + event-id integrity + `.sh` hostname), `FrequencyTables_ActorRenamed` (contributes successfully, exact renamed keys with preserved counts incl. a freq-only actor, `exam.Load` round-trip), `ActorNamedAdmin_NoFalseAbort`. **Non-vacuity proven per finding** — four probes (action scrub neutered, freq rename neutered, collision avoidance disabled, `sh` restored to the blocklist) each make their test fail; restored, all pass. Full `go build ./... && go test ./...` green; the pre-existing selfgate env-dependent failures did not fire.

**Honest limitation (documented, not silently dropped):** a bare, unshaped company fragment in a connector tool *name* or event *source* (e.g. `query_realcorp_audit` where "realcorp" is neither an actor nor part of any shaped identifier) is not detectable by shape patterns or the actor map. Wiring the fields into the walks catches every shaped or actor-derived occurrence (the description's hostname, actor fragments in names — both tested); the residue backstop for the shapeless case is the mandatory full-YAML operator review before `--yes`. A domain-label propagation pass (substring-replacing registrable labels harvested from scrubbed emails/hostnames) was considered and rejected: it would rewrite structural tokens like `github`/`azure` inside sources and freq keys and corrupt grading data.

## Review round 1 fixes (commit 5cd7222)

**[CRITICAL] Metadata never identifier-scrubbed — FIXED.** The identity substring pass AND the identifier scrub now run over every metadata string value and map key at any nesting depth (event metadata, finding metadata, connector_tool returns), through one shared hash cache so the same identifier maps to the same token everywhere — the reviewer's subscription UUID now carries the identical `id-<hash8>` token in the event target, `metadata.tenant`, and inside `metadata.resource_id`. New identifier shapes: hostnames/FQDNs (`host-<hash8>.example`, with a filename-extension filter so `policy.json` isn't shredded), IPv4 (`ip-<hash8>`), emails keep email shape (`user-<hash8>@example.com`), and a key net over identifier-carrying keys (email/ip/host/tenant/account/...) wholesale-tokenizes unrecognized-shape values **including bare numeric account ids**, which no string pattern can see. Raw payloads are stripped wholesale.

While fixing this, the new residue gate caught a second latent leak: **yaml.v3 propagates named map types (`exam.EventMetadata`) into nested `any` holes**, so every `case map[string]any:` type switch — including the C5 secret scrub's `scrubMetadataValue`, when reached via the yaml deep copy — silently skipped nested metadata blocks. Metadata trees are now normalized to plain `map[string]any`/`[]any` (reflection on Kind) immediately after the deep copy.

**[HIGH] Under-reporting consent diff — FIXED.** The diff is now the full redaction ledger: every actor/identifier rename enumerated (metadata renames included), secret redactions listed by document path (`events[0].metadata.github_token -> [REDACTED]` — paths, never values), counts printed from `len()` of the ledger slices. A transmit-time residue check (`verifyLedgerResidue`) grep-verifies every ledger original absent from **both** the sanitized YAML and the PR body and fails plan assembly closed on any hit — the PR body's "raw values never left" line is generated from that check passing, not asserted. The YAML header also no longer cites the operator's local scenario id (a hand-chosen `--id` can itself carry identifying content).

## Summary

- Registers two new chat tools in the existing `core/investigate` tool-calling loop (rd mallcoppro-a2f, C9): `run-eval` and `flag-like-this`. Both are thin adapters that self-exec the same `mallcop` binary the running process IS — never a parallel implementation of eval grading or scenario authoring.
- `run-eval` shells `mallcop eval --json` and answers "am I missing real attacks?" with `MY missed attacks: n of m (IDs); reference: x of y; false alarms: k` — local and reference numbers stay split, never blended. Returns an honest structured error (never a fabricated number) when the corpus/repo can't be resolved.
- `flag-like-this` shells `mallcop scenario capture ...` with the operator's stated must-fire/must-not-fire label, then confirms exactly what got written and where by parsing the real command's own confirmation output. Writes only to the operator's own repo/scenarios — propose-safe at every autonomy dial setting (stated explicitly in the tool description and the returned `RuntimeImpact`).
- Wires both into `serve.go`'s outbox trace summarizer, and documents the chat phrasing next to the CLI command in `README.md` and the scaffolded `scenarios/README.md` (`cli/deployrepo.go`) — the dual-audience contract.

## Deviation note

Per the C9 spec's constraint ("do NOT touch mallcop-pro in this slice ... verify and note"): I verified (read-only) that mallcop-pro's console proxies investigate tools generically — `docs/chat-investigate-protocol.md`'s `tool_call`/`tool_result` trace carries a bare tool name + summary string with no console-side tool allowlist found in `internal/server`. No mallcop-pro change is needed for these two tools to surface in the browser chat trace.

## Test plan

- [x] `go build ./...` green
- [x] `go test ./...` green (full suite, no skips/failures)
- [x] New pure unit tests: `evalArgs`/`captureArgs` arg-building, `parseCaptureOutput`, `runEvalSummary` (split-not-blended formatting), `summarizeToolResult` for both new tools, `ToolDefs()` schema presence

issue.title: test(eval): label all 38 unlabeled corpus scenarios + family coverage matrix (selfeval-c7)
issue.body:
## What

Label **all 38 previously-unlabeled pinned corpus scenarios** with `expected_detection`
ground truth, so `mallcop exam-detect` grades the full 58-scenario corpus instead of a
20-scenario toy. First denominator growth is free — label what already ships.

> **UPDATE (ground-truth review fix).** The first label set was REJECTED as output-tuned.
> This revision restores the dropped titular detector families and lets the affected rows go
> RED. **Recall dropped from 35/39 to 29/39 — that lower number is the honest one.** See
> "Honest gap inventory" below for the full RED list and the ground-truth reasoning.

| | labeled | unlabeled | recall (attacks caught) | precision (benign silent) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **before** (origin/main) | 20 | 38 | 15/16 = 93.8% | 4/4 = 100% |
| **first labels** (rejected) | 58 | 0 | 35/39 = 89.7% | 19/19 = 100% |
| **after** (honest relabel) | **58** | **0** | **29/39 = 74.4%** | **19/19 = 100%** |

- `exams/scenarios/corpus.pin` regenerated in the same change (count stays 58; sha256
  `1387e15e…` → `27c02ce0…`)
- `core/eval/coverage.go` — `CoverageMatrix(report)` rolls the graded rows up per detector
  family, exposed as an additive `coverage` field on the exam-detect JSON: the steering
  artifact for which thin family to grow next.

## Why the relabel (what the review caught)

Ground-truth discipline: **a label states what SHOULD fire given each scenario's
`trap_description` + threat, NEVER what `core/detect` currently emits.** The rejected labels
violated that: scenarios whose declared `detector:` / finding title names a family (e.g.
`unusual-timing`, `volume-anomaly`, `injection-probe`) were labeled with only the *co-firing*
family, dropping the titular family precisely because it cannot fire today. That kept rows
green by hiding real detector gaps — the exact thing the exam exists to surface. Honest
labeling adds the titular family and lets the row go RED; the red is the deliverable (the
self-heal loop closes it later — R9: never bend labels or detectors here).

## Honest gap inventory — the RED / open rows (self-heal targets)

exam-detect now exits 1 (open detection gaps). Per `.github/workflows/exam.yml` this is
**not** a merge blocker — the Tier-1 `exam-detect` check gates only on **exit 2**
(corpus.pin count/sha drift); exit 1 is "the loop's targets." **10 attacks are missed, 0
reserved** (every missing family is a *registered* detector, so `reserved:true` does not
apply):

| scenario | missing family | why it can't fire today | status |
|---|---|---|---|
| `UT-01-competing-signals` | `unusual-timing` | 03:14 role-grant; baseline has no actor-hours profile → `unusual_timing.go` returns nil (`!HasActorHours`). `priv-escalation` co-fires (green). | **NEW (relabel)** |
| `CO-01-newest-first` | `unusual-timing` | 03:14 role+key-creation; same actor-hours gap. `priv-escalation` co-fires. | **NEW (relabel)** |

issue.title: mallcoppro-65c4: mallcop scenario capture/lint — grow the local corpus from real telemetry
issue.body:
## Summary

- `mallcop scenario capture --store <dir> [--event-ids <ids>] [--actor <a> --window <dur>] --must-fire <family>|--must-not-fire <family> [--reserved]` — the author-independent ground-truth capture lane (db0's "flag things like this", corpus-expansion axis ii). Reads REAL stored events (core/store) and derives the baseline the SAME way core/pipeline.Run's step (1a) does (persisted KindBaseline snapshot merged with pkg/baseline.Build over every other stored event), then writes a schema-valid `provenance: captured` scenario YAML into scenarios/. Secret-shaped metadata values are redacted; actors/targets are kept (this file stays local). No inference calls; the output is DATA — never a detector or lookup rule (R2/R9).
- `mallcop scenario lint [--scenarios-dir <dir>] [--json]` — validates every scenarios/*.yaml parses via internal/exam.Load (the SAME loader `mallcop eval` uses), and warns (never blocks) when a locally-captured must_fire family has no must_not_fire twin anywhere in the directory — generalizing core/selfgate's L4c mandatory-twin gate from gate-time to authoring-time.
- `mallcop feedback dismiss` now prints a ready-to-run `scenario capture --must-not-fire` command for the matching benign twin (trivially additive UX pairing, per orchestrator notes).
- scenarios/README.md (cli/deployrepo.go) documents both commands.

Builds on mallcop PR #187 (C4: `mallcop eval`, provenance field, deploy-repo scenarios/ dir). Stays entirely inside `cli/`; does not touch `exams/scenarios/`, `corpus.pin`, or `core/eval/` (C7's turf, in flight separately).

## Test plan

- [x] `go build ./...` green
- [x] `go test ./cli/...` green (new: scenariocapture_test.go, scenariolint_test.go)
- [x] Full `go test ./...` green (baseline was already green on origin/main)
- [x] Round-trip test: capture from a seeded temp store, `internal/exam.Load` parses it, and grading through `eval.LoadExtraScenarios` + `eval.RunExamDetectOverCorpus` (the exact path `mallcop eval` uses) genuinely passes — the derived baseline excludes the captured actor and the registered `new-actor` detector fires for real.
- [x] Lint tests: a captured must_fire scenario with no twin prints the exact family + a capture recipe as a WARNING (command still exits 0); a paired must_fire/must_not_fire set prints no warning; a malformed scenario (missing `id`) is a hard error.
- [x] End-to-end verified against the built `mallcop` binary: `scan` → `scenario capture` (secret redaction confirmed) → `scenario lint` (warns) → `scenario capture --must-not-fire` (the twin) → `scenario lint` (clean) → `mallcop eval --json` (1/1 detected).

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

comment.body:
### Re-review REJECT addressed — four leak shapes closed (123bf17)

All four reviewer-proven leaks fixed in `cli/scenariocapture.go`:

1. **[HIGH] HTTP Basic auth** — added `(?i)basic\s+[A-Za-z0-9+/=]{16,}` to the whole-value pattern list (Bearer was covered, Basic was not; the base64 decodes straight to `user:password`).
2. **[HIGH] Stripe underscore keys** — added `sk_(live|test)_[a-zA-Z0-9]{16,}` and `rk_(live|test)_[a-zA-Z0-9]{16,}` (only hyphen `sk-` was covered).
3. **[MED] Colon-delimited creds** — new `captureColonSecretRE`, the `:` sibling of the k=v net, sharing one credential-key alternation (`captureSecretKeyAlt`). Catches both JSON-quoted (`"password":"hunter2json"`) and bare YAML/log (`password: topsecretyaml`) forms.
4. **[MED] Inline CLI-arg creds** — new `captureCLIDBPassRE` (blanks `-p<value>` on mysql/mariadb/psql/pg_dump-family command lines, command-name-guarded so a bare `-p\S+` doesn't shred unrelated flags) and `captureCLIUserPassRE` (blanks the whole `-u`/`--user` `user:pass` span, username included). `pass` added to the shared key list (`\b` keeps it off `bypass`).

Over-redaction bias restated in comments throughout.

**Tests.** New `TestScenarioCapture_RedactsRereviewLeakShapes` pushes all eight repro strings through the real capture path under keys that do NOT trip the key-substring net, then grep-asserts zero residue in the emitted YAML: the Basic base64, both Stripe keys, `hunter2json`, `topsecretyaml`, `hunter2cli`, `hunter2curl`, `hunter2pass`. Preservation assertions prove the in-string redactors stay surgical: `repo`, actor, `region=us-east-1`, the curl target host, and the `acme_db` mysql arg all survive, and the scenario still loads through `exam.Load`.

**Non-vacuity**: against the 77516ad scrub the new test fails on exactly all 8 residue assertions; passes with the fix. All prior assertions green, including the round-trip-through-eval test. Full `go build ./... && go test ./...` green (51 packages).

Note: the Stripe test fixtures are constructed at runtime (`"sk_live_" + strings.Repeat("A", 24)`) because GitHub push protection — correctly — blocks any commit containing a Stripe-key-shaped literal, fake or not. The scrubber only ever sees the assembled string.

Acknowledged residuals not chased per review: bare 40-char AWS secret under an innocuous key, sub-20-char bearer tokens, GCP JSON (PEM marker already caught).

issue.title: fix(investigate): sharpen extraction + 0-match recovery prompts (mallcoppro-110, mallcoppro-a20)
issue.body:
## Summary

Prompt/text-only fixes in `core/investigate/investigate.go` for two triage-lane quality bugs (no store/search logic touched — that's owned by mallcoppro-448):

- **mallcoppro-110** (deep-nested extraction): the analyst called `get_raw_event`, received the caller ARN and source IP in the payload, and still answered "not present … consult CloudTrail." Adds a dedicated "Extracting fields from a raw record" system-prompt section: scan the whole tool-result text for a field's key name as a substring before ever claiming absence; quote verbatim once found; never substitute a look-alike field (CloudTrail AssumeRole records carry both `userIdentity.arn` — the caller — and `requestParameters.roleArn`/`resources[].ARN` — the role being assumed *into* — which were getting confused). Adds a global anti-fabrication rule and explicit guidance for when the tool-result text visibly ends mid-structure: say the field "was not visible in what I received," never invent a plausible substitute, never punt to CloudTrail.
- **mallcoppro-a20** (0-match recovery): an unseeded "forge-proxy" question drove 4 wrong-axis `search_events`/`search_findings` guesses (`source=`, `type=`) against a store that held 100+ `actor=forge-proxy` events, then gave up. Adds explicit axis-pivot guidance: `actor`/`source`/`type` are separate, conjunctive filter axes — never guess two at once in the same call — and a hyphenated/slug-shaped name is virtually always an actor. Tuned for `DefaultMaxTurns=8`: guess the likely-right axis first, stop pivoting the moment a call returns real matches, treat an unfiltered recon pass as an optional last resort rather than a mandatory sweep (an earlier, more exhaustive draft measurably exceeded the turn budget before producing an answer).

## Live-replay evidence (real production store, real inference)

Built `./cmd/mallcop` from this branch, pointed `mallcop investigate --store <dir>` at a local clone of `3dl-dev/mallcop-deploy` branch `mallcop-findings` (real prod events/findings), against `https://api.mallcop.app` with `MALLCOP_MODEL=triage`:

- **mallcoppro-a20**, exact unseeded question ("give me the details of the forge-proxy external access. who did it? what was it?"): **3/3 clean passes** — each run pivots to `actor=forge-proxy`, finds the real critical `new-external-access` finding, answers with real (non-fabricated, verified-against-store) data.
- **mallcoppro-110**, deep-nested extraction on events whose raw payload stays under the tool-result box's 1024-char cap (e.g. `evt_95544befc02a`, 832 bytes): **10/10 clean, verbatim, correctly-disambiguated passes** across repeated rounds.
- **mallcoppro-110** on the event literally named in the bug report (`70f3898c…`, 2547-byte raw payload): improved from "confidently wrong every time" to "usually honest, occasionally still fabricates or mentions an external log" — **not** a reliable 3/3.

## Root cause found, NOT fixed here (out of scope)

The residual failure on `70f3898c…` traces to a pre-existing, unrelated code bug: `core/investigate`'s `runTools()` boxes *every* tool_result (not just `get_raw_event`'s) through `agent.WrapUntrusted`'s `maxFieldLen=1024` scalar-field cap (`core/agent/sanitize.go`) — a cap sized for a single attacker-controlled string (a finding title), wrongly applied to whole structured tool-result JSON blobs. This silently truncates any tool result over 1024 bytes before the model ever sees it — **99% of `get_raw_event` calls** against this store's real CloudTrail-shaped events (18,938 of 19,130 events checked). No prompt can make a model report a field it was never shown.

Filed as **mallcoppro-a1e** (p1, full evidence in the item notes) — `mallcoppro-110` cannot be fully closed until that cap is fixed.

Also filed, confirmed pre-existing and unrelated to this diff (reproduced identically on a stashed `origin/main` baseline):
- **mallcoppro-cc2** — `core/tools/github_actor` live tests flake under GitHub API rate limiting.
- **mallcoppro-655** — `core/pipeline`'s P50 latency test flakes under concurrent machine load.

## Test plan

- [x] `go build ./cmd/mallcop` — clean
- [x] `go test -count=1 ./...` — green except the two pre-existing, unrelated flakes above (confirmed via `git stash` baseline repro)
- [x] Live replay against real prod store + real inference, documented above
- [x] `gofmt -l` clean

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Only the CodeQL checks (which use a different trigger) ran and passed. This looks like a GitHub Actions dispatch/scheduling anomaly, not a workflow-file or permissions issue (workflows are `active`, my token has full repo access, no path filters apply to this diff).

To de-risk this, I ran every command `ci.yml` runs, locally, against this exact branch:
- `go build ./...` — clean
- `go vet ./...` — clean
- `go test -count=1 ./...` — green, except 2 confirmed pre-existing/unrelated flakes (reproduced identically on a `git stash`d baseline): `TestExecuteTool_DispatchesGithubActor`/`TestGithubActorLive_*` (GitHub API rate limiting — mallcoppro-cc2) and `TestPipeline_ScanLatency_P50OrchestrationOverheadIsSmall` (wall-clock bound under concurrent machine load — mallcoppro-655)
- `go test -tags docdemo -count=1 -v ./test/docdemo/...` — all pass
- `go test -tags e2e -count=1 -v ./cli/...` — all pass

Whoever picks this up for review/merge: please confirm the CI checks actually run before merging (may just need a maintainer-side re-trigger, or could be worth a look if it recurs on other PRs).

issue.title: fix(selfext): lockstep the output-cap raise (streamshim) + fail loudly on truncation
issue.body:
## Summary

Closes the lockstep + truncation-doom-loop gap tracked at rd `mallcoppro-da5`
(companion: `3dl-dev/mallcop-pro#<TBD>`).

- **`streamshim.MaxTokensCap` 4096 → 32768.** mallcop#201 (Adapter default) and
  forge#122 (`maxTokensCap`) already raised their caps to 32768 in lockstep, but
  a THIRD cap on the same wire path was missed: `streamshim.MaxTokensCap`.
  `mallcop-pro`'s `cmd/mallcop-ops/selfext.go` routes the donut rail through this
  shim ALWAYS and passes this constant as the clamp — silently re-truncating
  every request back down to 4096 regardless of what the Adapter declared to
  opencode. This was a **live gap on the production donut rail**, found while
  reconciling rd mallcoppro-da5 against the already-shipped mallcop#201/forge#122
  fixes.
- **Truncation guard.** Live-reproduced against the real `opencode-ai 1.17.11`
  binary (local fake server, deliberately truncated tool-call argument): opencode
  does not fail — it silently re-sends the identical oversized turn and relabels
  the malformed reply `tool="invalid"` (upstream sst/opencode#18108), 35+ times in
  45s, zero actionable stdout, until something external kills it. Added
  `scanTruncation` (schema-tolerant scan for `tool="invalid"` and/or a step-finish
  `reason="length"` event — either signal, even once) wired into `Invoke`: a
  truncated attempt now fails IMMEDIATELY with a loud, diagnosed error naming the
  configured cap, never retried.

**Lockstep value: 32768**, sourced from the coding-lane's authoring model max
output (measured live in rd mallcoppro-4a1's bisection — glm-5.2's reasoning
channel needs headroom beyond 4096 to think-then-write). All three caps
(`opencode.Adapter.defaultMaxOutputTokens`, forge `maxTokensCap`, and now
`streamshim.MaxTokensCap`) agree at 32768.

## Test plan

- [x] Baseline: `go test ./selfext/...` green before changes
- [x] `go build ./...` clean after changes
- [x] `go vet ./...` clean
- [x] `go test ./selfext/... ./cli/...` green after changes
- [x] `go test ./...` (full repo): green except 3 pre-existing, unrelated
      failures in `core/investigate`/`core/tools` (live GitHub API lookups,
      no network egress in the sandbox — confirmed on a clean origin/main
      checkout with zero diff; tracked at rd `mallcoppro-96f`, not touched here)
- [x] New tests: `TestScanTruncation` (table-driven, both signals + negatives),
      `TestInvokeFailsLoudlyOnTruncation`, `TestInvokeFailsLoudlyOnLengthFinishAlone`
      — prove the loud-error/never-retried contract end to end
- [x] `streamshim` test fixture bumped to a `max_tokens` value that still
      exceeds the new 32768 cap, so the clamp path stays exercised

The retry is +// gated by TWO hard conditions to avoid double-spend: +// +// - the worktree is still CLEAN (git status --porcelain empty) — proof +// nothing was authored; a run that wrote any file is never retried, and +// - the redacted transcript matches a TRANSIENT signal (see looksTransient) — +// a deterministic failure (bad model, config error, compile-time refusal) +// is not retried because a retry cannot help it. +// +// A canceled context or a spawn failure surfaces immediately (never retried). +func (a *Adapter) Invoke(ctx context.Context, wt *sandbox.Worktree, apiKey, task string) (Result, error) { + if wt == nil { + return Result{}, errors.New("opencode: worktree is nil") + } + if a.Lane == "" { + return Result{}, errors.New("opencode: Adapter.Lane is empty") + } + + cfg, err := a.ProviderConfig(apiKey, a.ForgeBaseURL) + if err != nil { + return Result{}, err + } + env := withConfigContent(wt.ScrubbedEnv(apiKey, a.ForgeBaseURL), cfg) + + maxAttempts := a.maxAttempts() + var res Result + for attempt := 1; attempt <= maxAttempts; attempt++ { + var runErr error + res, runErr = a.runOnce(ctx, wt, env, apiKey, task) + if runErr != nil { + // Spawn failure / context cancellation: surface it, never retry. + return res, runErr + } + if res.ExitCode == 0 || attempt == maxAttempts { + return res, nil + } + + // A timed-out attempt is NEVER retried: a hang is + // not the "transient, no-op fast-fail" this heuristic targets, so + // retrying would only risk stacking multiple bounded hangs instead of + // failing fast for the operator. + if res.TimedOut { + a.logger().Warn("opencode invocation timed out; not retried (fail fast on a hang)", + "attempt", attempt, "timeout", a.timeout()) + return res, nil + } + + // Non-zero exit with attempts remaining. Retry ONLY a transient, no-op + // fast-fail — and only when the worktree proves nothing was authored, so + // we never re-run over work that already spent inference. + clean, cerr := worktreeClean(ctx, wt.Dir) + if cerr != nil || !clean { + a.logger().Info("opencode non-zero exit; not retried (authored files or indeterminate worktree)", + "exit_code", res.ExitCode, "attempt", attempt, "worktree_clean_err", cerr) + return res, nil + } + if !looksTransient(res.TranscriptRedacted) { + a.logger().Info("opencode non-zero exit; not retried (non-transient failure)", + "exit_code", res.ExitCode, "attempt", attempt, "transcript_bytes", len(res.TranscriptRedacted)) + return res, nil + } + a.logger().Warn("opencode transient fast-fail; retrying", + "exit_code", res.ExitCode, "attempt", attempt, "next_attempt", attempt+1, + "max_attempts", maxAttempts, "transcript_bytes", len(res.TranscriptRedacted)) + a.sleep(a.retryBackoff()) + } + return res, nil +} + +// runOnce performs a SINGLE headless opencode invocation and captures its +// redacted transcript, extracted files, and exit code. It is the retry unit for +// Invoke. A spawn failure / canceled (by the CALLER, not our own timeout) +// context is returned as an error (with the redacted transcript captured so +// far); a non-zero process exit is recorded in Result.ExitCode, not returned +// as an error. +// +// # Bounded wall-clock +// +// Every attempt gets its OWN context.WithTimeout(ctx, a.timeout()) layered on +// top of the caller's ctx — a live run has wedged the whole build loop for +// ~10h with nothing bounding it, since the caller's own ctx (context.Background() +// at the CLI) never times out on its own. On expiry the WHOLE PROCESS GROUP is +// killed (setProcessGroup — mirroring mallcop connect/exec's procgroup +// pattern: a headless opencode may fork tool subprocesses that inherit the +// stdout/stderr pipes, so killing only the direct child could leave Wait +// blocked on a pipe a grandchild still holds open) and cmd.WaitDelay bounds +// how long Wait can then take to observe that. A timeout is recorded in +// Result.TimedOut, NOT returned as an error — same shape as any other +// non-zero-exit run — so it flows through the engine's existing +// failWithTranscript diagnostics path. +func (a *Adapter) runOnce(ctx context.Context, wt *sandbox.Worktree, env []string, apiKey, task string) (Result, error) { + runCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, a.timeout()) + defer cancel() + + model := a.provider() + "/" + a.model() + args := []string{ + "run", task, + "-m", model, + "--format", "json", + "--dangerously-skip-permissions", + "--dir", wt.Dir, + } + args = append(args, a.extraRunArgs...) + + // Build the command. When Confine is set, spawn opencode under OS-enforced + // Landlock confinement via the mallcop-ops re-exec launcher (jail.WrapCommand + // runs /proc/self/exe, whose main() calls jail.MaybeReexec to apply the jail + // and then exec opencode). FAIL-CLOSED: if the kernel cannot establish the + // jail, refuse to author rather than spawn opencode unconfined. + var cmd *exec.Cmd + if a.Confine { + if serr := jail.Supported(); serr != nil { + return Result{}, fmt.Errorf("opencode: OS-enforced authoring jail required but unavailable: %w", serr) + } + pol, perr := jailPolicy(wt, a.ForgeBaseURL) + if perr != nil { + return Result{}, perr + } + penv, perr := jail.PolicyEnv(pol) + if perr != nil { + return Result{}, perr + } + cmd = jail.WrapCommand(runCtx, "/proc/self/exe", a.bin(), args...) + env = append(env, penv) + } else { + cmd = exec.CommandContext(runCtx, a.bin(), args...) + } + cmd.Env = env + cmd.Dir = wt.Dir + setProcessGroup(cmd) + cmd.WaitDelay = invokeWaitDelay + + var stdout, stderr bytes.Buffer + cmd.Stdout = &stdout + cmd.Stderr = &stderr + + runErr := cmd.Run() + timedOut := errors.Is(runCtx.Err(), context.DeadlineExceeded) + + // Redact BEFORE anything is returned for persistence. + raw := stdout.String() + if stderr.Len() > 0 { + raw += "\n--- stderr ---\n" + stderr.String() + } + if timedOut { + raw += fmt.Sprintf("\n--- opencode killed: exceeded timeout %s ---\n", a.timeout()) + } + redacted := redact.Redact(raw, apiKey) + + files, text := Parse(stdout.Bytes()) + + exitCode := 0 + if runErr != nil { + var exitErr *exec.ExitError + if errors.As(runErr, &exitErr) { + // The process ran and exited non-zero (including signal-killed by + // our own timeout): not an adapter error. + exitCode = exitErr.ExitCode() + } else if timedOut { + // The kill raced Wait in a way that didn't surface as a plain + // *exec.ExitError (e.g. WaitDelay force-closed the pipes) — still + // OUR OWN bound firing, not a spawn failure. Record it, don't error. + exitCode = -1 + } else { + // Spawn failure / context cancellation the CALLER initiated: surface it. + return Result{ + TranscriptRedacted: []byte(redacted), + ExitCode: -1, + }, fmt.Errorf("opencode: run %s: %w", a.bin(), runErr) + } + } + + a.logger().Info("opencode invocation complete", + "exit_code", exitCode, + "authored_files", len(files), + "transcript_bytes", len(redacted), + "timed_out", timedOut, + ) + + return Result{ + AuthoredFiles: files, + AssistantText: text, + TranscriptRedacted: []byte(redacted), + ExitCode: exitCode, + TimedOut: timedOut, + }, nil +} + +// transientEmptyThreshold is the transcript size (bytes, trimmed) below which a +// non-zero-exit run is treated as an empty/near-empty upstream fast-fail. The +// observed live fast-fail is a ~519-byte transcript, so this covers the +// "opencode produced almost nothing and gave up" shape even absent an explicit +// status code. +const transientEmptyThreshold = 800 + +// transientPatterns match a transcript that indicates a TRANSIENT upstream +// failure (a 5xx status, a rate-limit, a timeout, a dropped connection, or an +// explicit "overloaded / try again" signal) — the fast-fail worth retrying. +// They are deliberately conservative: none match a substantive authoring +// failure (a compile error, a policy refusal, a tool error), so a run that did +// real work is not retried. +var transientPatterns = []*regexp.Regexp{ + regexp.MustCompile(`(?i)\b(50[0-9]|429)\b`), + regexp.MustCompile(`(?i)rate.?limit|too many requests`), + regexp.MustCompile(`(?i)timeout|timed out|deadline exceeded`), + regexp.MustCompile(`(?i)connection (reset|refused|closed)|unexpected eof|no response|empty response`), + regexp.MustCompile(`(?i)temporarily unavailable|service unavailable|overloaded|please try again`), +} + +// looksTransient reports whether a non-zero-exit transcript indicates a +// transient upstream hiccup worth one more attempt. An empty/near-empty +// transcript is itself a transient signal (opencode produced no usable event +// stream before giving up). +func looksTransient(transcript []byte) bool { + if len(bytes.TrimSpace(transcript)) < transientEmptyThreshold { + return true + } + for _, re := range transientPatterns { + if re.Match(transcript) { + return true + } + } + return false +} + +// worktreeClean reports whether the worktree has NO staged/unstaged changes — +// the authoritative "authored nothing" signal that gates a retry. Any error +// determining cleanliness returns (false, err): when in doubt, do NOT retry. +func worktreeClean(ctx context.Context, dir string) (bool, error) { + cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", "-C", dir, "status", "--porcelain") + // Scrub the env to the bare minimum: git needs none of the operator + // credentials, and this call must not depend on the caller's config. + cmd.Env = []string{"PATH=" + os.Getenv("PATH"), "GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1", "GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0"} + out, err := cmd.Output() + if err != nil { + return false, fmt.Errorf("opencode: git status: %w", err) + } + return len(bytes.TrimSpace(out)) == 0, nil +} + +// withConfigContent returns env with the OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT entry replaced +// (or appended) with cfg. Every other entry — the sandbox's credential-scrubbed +// allowlist — is preserved verbatim, so this override cannot widen the env. +func withConfigContent(env []string, cfg string) []string { + const key = "OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT=" + out := make([]string, 0, len(env)+1)

issue.title: fix(reusable): self-enforced egress jail (ruling d9d, option iii) + checksum toolchain + --exam-repo
issue.body:
## Self-enforced egress jail + exam-repo fix for the CODE-lane reusable workflow

Implements **rd mallcoppro-d9d** (Baron's ruling on the escalation), building on
**mallcoppro-1a1** for **mallcoppro-10e**, and fixes **mallcoppro-364** in the same pass.

### Path to this design
1. **Container removal (was RULING B / 1a1).** harden-runner cannot enforce egress
   inside a `container:` job, so the CODE lane could never author on GitHub-hosted
   runners (evidence: mallcop-e2e run `29314104398`). Removed `container:` from both jobs
   and reproduced the runner image's toolchain **pre-jail** from SHA-256-verified public
   downloads.
2. **harden-runner on the host — live-proof discovered a second wall** (run `29421569762`):
   harden-runner block mode is a **StepSecurity paid feature on PRIVATE repos**; a
   free-tier private repo (mallcop-e2e) silently downgrades to **audit** and cannot block.
   The fail-closed proof correctly refused to author.
3. **RULING d9d — option (iii): self-enforce the jail.** Drop harden-runner / StepSecurity
   entirely; enforce egress with a hand-rolled iptables default-DENY ruleset that works on
   the free tier, private repos included.

### The self-enforced jail (both jobs, one boundary step)
Applied AFTER all checksum-verified toolchain setup + `go mod download` + checkouts, and
BEFORE anything model-driven:
- Resolve the allowlist to IPs while DNS is still open, then load an **atomic
  `iptables-restore`** ruleset: `OUTPUT` policy **DROP**, permitting only
  - loopback,
  - `ESTABLISHED,RELATED` return traffic (keeps the runner's live connection),
  - the DNS resolver(s) on `:53` (incl. the real systemd-resolved upstream),
  - the pinned **app / github / go-proxy** IPs on `:443`,
  - the **GitHub Actions runner control-plane** ranges on `:443` (`api.github.com/meta`
    `.actions`) — on a host runner the jail governs the runner agent, which must keep
    reaching the Actions service or the job is marked lost.
- **IPv6** new-egress dropped (loopback + established only).
- **SUDO DESTROYED** (`chmod 0000` the setuid binary) so authored/model-driven code — the
  threat model, which has passwordless sudo on GH-hosted runners — cannot flush the rules
  and lift its own jail.

### Fail-closed proof (extended, semantics kept)
Planted `curl` to a non-allowlisted host **must be blocked** + inference endpoint **must
be reachable** + **`sudo -n true` must now fail**. Any of the three failing → exit
non-zero, author nothing.

### Defense in depth / documented residual
The coarse IP jail cannot distinguish processes, so the runner-control-plane allowance is
broad (GitHub-owned Azure ranges). The genuinely **untrusted** process — the opencode
child — is separately confined by the **fine per-process Landlock network jail**
mallcop-ops applies (mallcoppro-6c4), restricting it to the inference endpoint. So
model-driven code cannot use the runner-infra surface.

### exam-repo (mallcoppro-364), unchanged from the prior revision
Check out `mallcop-app/mallcop@v0.9.3` (`cmd/mallcop` + `exams/scenarios/corpus.pin`, same
tag as the pinned gate binary) into `_exam` and pass `--exam-repo`. Ignored when the
target ships its own `cmd/mallcop`, so always safe.

### Validation
Proven live on a **branch** of `mallcop-app/mallcop-e2e` (never main). Success criteria:
(a) egress proof passes all three assertions on the **private** repo (now works free-tier);
(b) the run reaches the gate stages with `--exam-repo` consulted (no reference-tree
rejection). Run link + per-step outcomes in a follow-up comment.

**Do not merge without human review** — security-sensitive supply-chain / egress change.

rd **mallcoppro-d9d** (ruling) · **mallcoppro-10e** · **mallcoppro-364**

comment.body:
## Live-proof result — self-enforced jail (ruling d9d), run 29426418896

Branch `work/selfext-egress-b-proof` of `mallcop-app/mallcop-e2e` (**private repo**),
caller pinned to this branch head `8758475`. One `workflow_dispatch`, rail `donut-byoi`,
$2 budget.

### (a) EGRESS JAIL — PROVEN on the private repo (free tier)
Per-step outcomes (author job):
- steps 2–9 (checkouts + checksum-verified toolchain + go mod download): **success**
- step 10 `apply self-enforced egress jail + destroy sudo`: **success**
- step 11 `verify egress jail (fail-closed — blocked + reachable + sudo dead)`: **success**

Step 11 is **fail-closed** (exit non-zero if ANY assertion fails), so its green
conclusion proves all three: planted `curl https://example.com` **blocked**, inference
endpoint **reachable**, and `sudo -n true` **fails** (jail un-liftable). This is the
result harden-runner could not deliver on a private repo (it downgraded to audit) — the
hand-rolled iptables jail enforces on the free tier. The runner also stayed healthy under
the jail (step results reported), confirming the `meta.actions` runner-control-plane
allowance works.

### (b) EXAM-REPO / mallcoppro-364 — PROVEN
- CI step 4 `checkout the reference mallcop tree (mallcop-app/mallcop@v0.9.3)`: **success**
- Deterministic **$0** gate reproduction (no inference), `mallcop validate-proposal` on an
  authored `detectors/authored-deploy-burst/` diff in the customer-shaped mallcop-e2e tree:

  | run | guard stage | result |
  |-----|-------------|--------|
  | **without** `--exam-repo` | **FAIL — rule `code-frozen`** ("addition of a .go file under detectors/: detectors/ has no sanctioned Go code lane") | the 364 bug |
  | **with** `--exam-repo <mallcop@v0.9.3>` | **PASS (0 findings)** → structural PASS (`go build`/`go vet` OK) → stage 3 "customer-tree exam **via reference tree**" | 364 fixed |

  With `--exam-repo` the guard's code-frozen rejection disappears and the gate grades the
  authored detector against the reference tree. (The exam-detect stage then reports
  `customer-tree-exam-fail` only because the fixture is a trivial string-rename copy whose
  Go logic doesn't fire on the renamed scenarios — a fixture artifact; the load-bearing
  fact is that grading now *proceeds via the reference tree* instead of rejecting.)

### Notes
- The run cancelled at step 12 (authoring) on the wall-clock backstop — opencode on
  metered inference is slow. A full authoring completion was a bonus, not a criterion.
- Archived CI logs are empty: the jail (correctly) does not allowlist the Actions
  blob-log endpoint, so the post-job log archive upload is dropped. Step **conclusions**
  (via the API) are the evidence; step 11's fail-closed contract makes its green
  conclusion sufficient for (a). Follow-up option: allowlist the Actions results/blob
  endpoint if readable in-run logs are wanted (costs a small egress widening).

The mallcop **self-extension CODE lane** authored a new offline detector, `authored-deploy-flood`, entirely via nested **opencode (GLM-5.2)** on metered inference in a sandboxed worktree — then gated it. This PR is the human-review artifact.

- `exams/scenarios/authored/deployflood-benign-twin.yaml` — proves it stays silent on a benign look-alike

## Safety

comment.body:
## Real flood semantics (rd mallcoppro-8ac9, ruled by Baron 2026-07-15)

**Do not merge without human review** — this remains a GATED self-authored detector.

### The bug

`authored-deploy-flood` fired severity:high on **every single** `github.deployment` event — no counting, no window, no baseline. Despite the name and docs ("a flood of deployments"), it was a false-positive cannon: any normal deploy on any customer repo would have escalated. The old benign-twin only proved a *different event type* (`github.push`) stays silent — it never proved a single legitimate deployment stays silent, which it did not.

### The fix

`Detect` (`core/detect/authored/deployflood/deployflood.go`) now counts `github.deployment` events per actor across the given event set and compares the count against that actor's baseline deployment frequency via `pkg/baseline.Baseline.FreqCountActor("github", "github.deployment", actor)` — the same 3-segment `source:event_type:actor` key shape the corpus `frequency_tables` and the framework's `volume-anomaly` detector both use (mirrored, not invented).

It fires only on a genuine burst:
- `count >= 8` (absolute floor) **regardless of baseline** — a flood with no history still fires, or
- `count > 3 × baseline` once the baseline is established (`>= 3`, so a thin baseline can't be gamed into a "3×" false alarm off noise).

A single deployment, or a volume the baseline already explains, never fires. Severity stays `high`, but only for a real flood. Stays pure (no I/O, no package-state mutation, read-only over `events`/`bl`) — passes the K7 shape gate and the K2a import allow-list unchanged.

### Scenarios rewritten

- **must-fire**: 10 `github.deployment` events from one actor (`burst-actor`) against a zero baseline — a genuine burst.
- **benign-twin**: **one** `github.deployment` event from an actor with an established baseline (5) — this is the key fix: the benign is now a real deployment, not a different event type, so the gate actually tests flood-vs-single.

issue.title: fix(reusable): self-enforced egress jail (ruling d9d, option iii) + checksum toolchain + --exam-repo
issue.body:
## Self-enforced egress jail + exam-repo fix for the CODE-lane reusable workflow

Implements **rd mallcoppro-d9d** (Baron's ruling on the escalation), building on
**mallcoppro-1a1** for **mallcoppro-10e**, and fixes **mallcoppro-364** in the same pass.

### Path to this design
1. **Container removal (was RULING B / 1a1).** harden-runner cannot enforce egress
   inside a `container:` job, so the CODE lane could never author on GitHub-hosted
   runners (evidence: mallcop-e2e run `29314104398`). Removed `container:` from both jobs
   and reproduced the runner image's toolchain **pre-jail** from SHA-256-verified public
   downloads.
2. **harden-runner on the host — live-proof discovered a second wall** (run `29421569762`):
   harden-runner block mode is a **StepSecurity paid feature on PRIVATE repos**; a
   free-tier private repo (mallcop-e2e) silently downgrades to **audit** and cannot block.
   The fail-closed proof correctly refused to author.
3. **RULING d9d — option (iii): self-enforce the jail.** Drop harden-runner / StepSecurity
   entirely; enforce egress with a hand-rolled iptables default-DENY ruleset that works on
   the free tier, private repos included.

### The self-enforced jail (both jobs, one boundary step)
Applied AFTER all checksum-verified toolchain setup + `go mod download` + checkouts, and
BEFORE anything model-driven:
- Resolve the allowlist to IPs while DNS is still open, then load an **atomic
  `iptables-restore`** ruleset: `OUTPUT` policy **DROP**, permitting only
  - loopback,
  - `ESTABLISHED,RELATED` return traffic (keeps the runner's live connection),
  - the DNS resolver(s) on `:53` (incl. the real systemd-resolved upstream),
  - the pinned **app / github / go-proxy** IPs on `:443`,
  - the **GitHub Actions runner control-plane** ranges on `:443` (`api.github.com/meta`
    `.actions`) — on a host runner the jail governs the runner agent, which must keep
    reaching the Actions service or the job is marked lost.
- **IPv6** new-egress dropped (loopback + established only).
- **SUDO DESTROYED** (`chmod 0000` the setuid binary) so authored/model-driven code — the
  threat model, which has passwordless sudo on GH-hosted runners — cannot flush the rules
  and lift its own jail.

### Fail-closed proof (extended, semantics kept)
Planted `curl` to a non-allowlisted host **must be blocked** + inference endpoint **must
be reachable** + **`sudo -n true` must now fail**. Any of the three failing → exit
non-zero, author nothing.

### Defense in depth / documented residual
The coarse IP jail cannot distinguish processes, so the runner-control-plane allowance is
broad (GitHub-owned Azure ranges). The genuinely **untrusted** process — the opencode
child — is separately confined by the **fine per-process Landlock network jail**
mallcop-ops applies (mallcoppro-6c4), restricting it to the inference endpoint. So
model-driven code cannot use the runner-infra surface.

### exam-repo (mallcoppro-364), unchanged from the prior revision
Check out `mallcop-app/mallcop@v0.9.3` (`cmd/mallcop` + `exams/scenarios/corpus.pin`, same
tag as the pinned gate binary) into `_exam` and pass `--exam-repo`. Ignored when the
target ships its own `cmd/mallcop`, so always safe.

### Validation
Proven live on a **branch** of `mallcop-app/mallcop-e2e` (never main). Success criteria:
(a) egress proof passes all three assertions on the **private** repo (now works free-tier);
(b) the run reaches the gate stages with `--exam-repo` consulted (no reference-tree
rejection). Run link + per-step outcomes in a follow-up comment.

**Do not merge without human review** — security-sensitive supply-chain / egress change.

rd **mallcoppro-d9d** (ruling) · **mallcoppro-10e** · **mallcoppro-364**

comment.body:
## Live-proof result (mallcop-e2e branch `work/selfext-egress-b-proof`, run 29421569762)

Dispatched one `workflow_dispatch` against a branch of `mallcop-app/mallcop-e2e`
pinned to this branch head (`d3f7c10`). Rail `donut-byoi`, budget $2, detector
`authored-deploy-burst` / `github.deployment`. **Result: author job failed at the
egress-jail proof — but far past where the container version died, and $0 spend
(authoring never ran).**

### What this PR proved works (all green on a bare GitHub-hosted runner)
- Toolchain reproduction pre-jail: opencode `@1.17.11` (pinned, `--ignore-scripts`),
  Go 1.25 (setup-go), Node 24 (setup-node), `mallcop-ops` + `mallcop` from
  **SHA-256-verified** release tarballs (`sha256sum -c` passed), bundled config.
- `--exam-repo` reference tree checkout: `mallcop-app/mallcop@v0.9.3` → `_exam` (green).
- Opener-scripts checkout via `github.job_workflow_sha` → `_selfext` (green).
- `go mod download` pre-fetch (green).
- harden-runner planted (green). **The fail-closed egress proof then correctly
  refused to author under an unproven jail — the gate works as designed.**

Contrast with the container run `29314104398`, which died at step 6 (egress proof)
because harden-runner cannot enforce egress inside a container. RULING B's container
removal is validated: we now get all the way to the jail-proof step.

### Two blockers discovered (both require a design/infra decision — NOT code bugs)

**A. `mallcop-e2e` is a PRIVATE repo → harden-runner block mode is a paid-tier
feature for private repos.** The pre-step config logged `"private":true`,
`"api_key":""`; the agent initialized in **audit** mode (`NewAuditClient created`,
`added audit rules`) despite `egress_policy:block`, enforcing only the global
malicious-IP blocklist. The planted `curl https://example.com` was logged but **not
blocked** → fail-closed proof (correctly) failed. Ref: StepSecurity docs — "Private
repository support ... is part of the platform's paid tier."

**B. harden-runner enforces from the job-start pre-hook, not from its step
position.** Per StepSecurity: it "installs eBPF hooks at the kernel level before any
user-defined workflow steps execute." So placing the pinned toolchain downloads
*before* the harden-runner step does NOT run them outside the jail. Under **real**
block enforcement (public repo / paid tier) the pre-jail download hosts (npm
registry, nodejs.org, Go dist, opencode release) — which RULING B said not to
allowlist — would be **blocked**, breaking the toolchain install. The "downloads
pre-jail, jail after via step ordering" model is not achievable with harden-runner.

### Recommendation (needs a ruling)
- **Enforcement:** either (i) enable a StepSecurity subscription for the org's
  private repos, or (ii) run the live proof on a public dogfood repo, or (iii) drop
  the harden-runner dependency and self-enforce egress (nftables default-deny) —
  which also resolves B.
- **For B specifically:** split into two jobs — an un-jailed `setup` job that
  reproduces + **caches** the toolchain and Go modules, and a `author` job with
  harden-runner as the true first step (jail from job start) that restores the cache
  and runs authoring under the minimal allowlist. This is the only way to keep the
  allowlist free of download hosts while the jail is up from job start.

This PR faithfully implements RULING B as written and is correct for audit-mode /
container-removal purposes; findings A and B mean a follow-up ruling is needed before
a green *block-enforced* proof is possible. **Do not merge without that decision.**

issue.title: feat(cli): scenario contribute — the opt-in commons (mallcoppro-c78, C8)
issue.body:
## Summary

Implements C8 (rd `mallcoppro-c78`) — corpus-expansion axis iii, the OPT-IN
commons: `mallcop scenario contribute <scenarios/file.yaml>`.

- **Sandbox**: `sanitizeScenarioForContribution` deep-copies the local
  scenario (yaml round-trip, never touches the source file) and runs a
  deterministic two-pass sanitize:
  1. **Identity pass** — every distinct actor found anywhere in the document
     (events, finding metadata, actor_chain, baseline known_entities/
     actor_roles/actor_hours/relationships) is renamed to a canonical
     corpus-style token (`ci-bot`, `admin-user`, ... — first-seen order,
     20-token pool with a content-hash fallback), including a longest-first
     substring pass over prose fields so a name mentioned in free text
     doesn't survive.
  2. **Identifier pass** — residual UUIDs / emails / long all-hex runs
     (e.g. an Azure subscription id) get a deterministic `sub-<hash8>` /
     `id-<hash8>` token, matching VA-03's `sub-<hex8>` convention. Built as a
     single non-overlapping pass over the *original* string (not chained
     regex replacements) so an inserted hash token can never be re-matched
     and re-hashed by a later pass.
  - Secret-shaped metadata values are redacted by **reusing**
    `scrubPayloadMap` from `cli/scenariocapture.go` (C5 #190) — not forked.
  - Timestamps are shifted by one constant duration so every relative delta
    (fine event spacing *and* multi-month baseline relationship history) is
    preserved exactly, anchored so the earliest event lands on
    `2026-03-10T08:00:00Z` (VA-03's own start).
- **Gate**: `provenance: authored` scenarios are refused by default
  (author-independence — the commons should predominantly grow from
  operator/captured ground truth); `--allow-authored` overrides.
- **PR**: corpus.pin is regenerated against the manifest-relative `RelPath`
  convention `core/eval/corpus.go`'s loader actually uses (relative to
  `exams/scenarios/`, not the full path — this was caught by a test that
  round-trips the regenerated pin through the real `eval.Load`). Opens via
  `gh` (fork + branch + commit + push + `gh pr create`) when available, else
  prints exact manual instructions. Nothing auto-merges (mallcop-pro d70
  ruling: contribute-back stays reviewed).
- `--dry-run` prints the full redaction diff (local review — original
  values, since nothing has left the machine) and the would-be PR content,
  then returns *before* any git/gh invocation is reachable. The PR body
  itself carries only counts derived from the diff, never raw original
  actor/target values, since the PR body does leave the machine.

## Safety

`openContributePR` is the **only** function that touches git/gh/network,
reachable only from the non-dry-run `--yes` path. No test in
`scenariocontribute_test.go` calls it — every test either exercises
`runScenarioContribute` with `--dry-run` (which structurally returns before
that function is reachable) or calls the pure plan-assembly functions
directly.

## Test plan

- [x] `go build ./...` clean
- [x] `go vet ./...` clean
- [x] `go test ./cli/...` — 7 new targeted tests green:
  - `TestScenarioContribute_PinRegenCorrectness` — round-trips the
    regenerated pin through the *real* `eval.Load`, not a hand-duplicated
    hash check
  - `TestScenarioContribute_SanitizeRoundTrip` — grep-class no-residue +
    over-redaction guards + exact preserved relative timing
  - `TestScenarioContribute_SanitizedScenarioParsesViaExamLoad`
  - `TestScenarioContribute_AuthoredRefusal_AndOverride`
  - `TestScenarioContribute_DryRun_PrintsRedactionDiffAndPRContent`
  - `TestScenarioContribute_NoYesNoDryRun_StopsWithoutConfirming`
  - `TestScenarioContribute_NoExpectedDetection_Errors`
- [x] `go test ./...` — full suite green (58 packages), including the
      known-flaky `core/tools` LIVE GitHub test (passed clean, no isolation
      needed)
- [x] Manual smoke test: `mallcop scenario contribute --dry-run` against a
      captured-style fixture with real emails/tokens/subscription ids —
      confirmed no residue in the printed sanitized YAML and correct
      `count 58 -> 59` pin delta against the real embedded reference corpus

comment.body:
## Review round 2 fixes (commit c4e03a3)

**[HIGH-1] Sanitizer-blind struct fields — FIXED.** Event `id:`, event `action:` (the promoted-payload case), `actor_chain[].action`, `connector_tools[].name`/`description`, and `tags[]` are all wired into both the actor-substring pass and the identifier scrub. Event ids get **shape-preserving span tokenization**: only identifier-shaped substrings are replaced (`azure-<uuid>-000123` → `azure-id-<hash8>-000123`), through the document-wide shared hash cache — ordering and uniqueness survive, and `finding.event_ids` receives the byte-identical transform so the cross-reference stays intact (asserted).

**[HIGH-2] frequency_tables actor segments — FIXED.** Keys get exact per-segment actor renames (position-independent — handles both `source:event_type:actor` and the extended `source:event_type:actor:N:period` per `pkg/baseline`'s ActorTypeCount construction; count values are never touched) plus the identifier scrub. Actors appearing **only** in freq keys (segment index 2) are now collected into the actor map, so an aged-out-but-baselined actor renames everywhere. The regression test proves a captured-with-baseline scenario — the primary feedstock — contributes successfully end-to-end through the real dry-run path, with renamed keys, preserved counts, and an `exam.Load` round-trip.

**[MED-1] Pool-token false abort — FIXED.** `buildContributeActorMap` now skips pool tokens that contain or are contained by any collected actor original (≥3 bytes, matching the gate's own skip); the hash fallback salts deterministically until conflict-free. An actor literally named `admin` no longer lands anyone on `admin-user`/`infra-admin`, so the gate's substring check stays sound. The gate's error message now names the tokenizer-collision cause for the theoretically-unreachable residual case instead of misdiagnosing it as a leak.

**[MED-2] Real-TLD blocklist collisions — FIXED.** `sh`, `md`, `rs`, `py`, and `zip` (all real TLDs) are removed from the filename-extension filter — `status.realcorp.sh` now tokenizes to `host-<hash8>.example` and appears in the ledger. Dotted filenames with those endings get hostname-tokenized instead: over-redaction bias, and the ledger shows the operator exactly what was replaced. Non-TLD extensions (`js`, `go`, `gz`, `db`, ...) stay filtered so ordinary filenames survive.

**Tests.** Three new regressions built from the reviewer's proven-leak shapes, all through the real `runScenarioContribute --dry-run` path: `AuxiliaryFieldLeaks_Scrubbed` (grep-class residue over both transmit artifacts + ledger enumeration + event-id integrity + `.sh` hostname), `FrequencyTables_ActorRenamed` (contributes successfully, exact renamed keys with preserved counts incl. a freq-only actor, `exam.Load` round-trip), `ActorNamedAdmin_NoFalseAbort`. **Non-vacuity proven per finding** — four probes (action scrub neutered, freq rename neutered, collision avoidance disabled, `sh` restored to the blocklist) each make their test fail; restored, all pass. Full `go build ./... && go test ./...` green; the pre-existing selfgate env-dependent failures did not fire.

**Honest limitation (documented, not silently dropped):** a bare, unshaped company fragment in a connector tool *name* or event *source* (e.g. `query_realcorp_audit` where "realcorp" is neither an actor nor part of any shaped identifier) is not detectable by shape patterns or the actor map. Wiring the fields into the walks catches every shaped or actor-derived occurrence (the description's hostname, actor fragments in names — both tested); the residue backstop for the shapeless case is the mandatory full-YAML operator review before `--yes`. A domain-label propagation pass (substring-replacing registrable labels harvested from scrubbed emails/hostnames) was considered and rejected: it would rewrite structural tokens like `github`/`azure` inside sources and freq keys and corrupt grading data.

## Review round 1 fixes (commit 5cd7222)

**[CRITICAL] Metadata never identifier-scrubbed — FIXED.** The identity substring pass AND the identifier scrub now run over every metadata string value and map key at any nesting depth (event metadata, finding metadata, connector_tool returns), through one shared hash cache so the same identifier maps to the same token everywhere — the reviewer's subscription UUID now carries the identical `id-<hash8>` token in the event target, `metadata.tenant`, and inside `metadata.resource_id`. **[HIGH] Under-reporting consent diff — FIXED.** The diff is now the full redaction ledger: every actor/identifier rename enumerated (metadata renames included), secret redactions listed by document path (`events[0].metadata.github_token -> [REDACTED]` — paths, never values), counts printed from `len()` of the ledger slices. A transmit-time residue check (`verifyLedgerResidue`) grep-verifies every ledger original absent from **both** the sanitized YAML and the PR body and fails plan assembly closed on any hit — the PR body's "raw values never left" line is generated from that check passing, not asserted. The YAML header also no longer cites the operator's local scenario id (a hand-chosen `--id` can itself carry identifying content).

**Tests.** The reviewer's fixture shapes are now `TestScenarioContribute_MetadataIdentifierLeaks_Scrubbed`: grep-class residue assertions over both transmit artifacts (coworker emails under `peer_email`+`collaborator`, private hostname twice incl. nested, internal IP, string+numeric account ids, UUID x3, `realcorp` as a fragment), ledger-enumeration assertions, same-token agreement, over-redaction guards (`blobs_accessed: 80` and `us-east-1` survive), and the sub-second delta. **Non-vacuity proven**: with the metadata scrub disabled the test fails — and the residue gate independently fails the plan closed. ## Summary

- Registers two new chat tools in the existing `core/investigate` tool-calling loop (rd mallcoppro-a2f, C9): `run-eval` and `flag-like-this`. Both are thin adapters that self-exec the same `mallcop` binary the running process IS — never a parallel implementation of eval grading or scenario authoring.
- `run-eval` shells `mallcop eval --json` and answers "am I missing real attacks?" with `MY missed attacks: n of m (IDs); reference: x of y; false alarms: k` — local and reference numbers stay split, never blended. Returns an honest structured error (never a fabricated number) when the corpus/repo can't be resolved.
- `flag-like-this` shells `mallcop scenario capture ...` with the operator's stated must-fire/must-not-fire label, then confirms exactly what got written and where by parsing the real command's own confirmation output. Writes only to the operator's own repo/scenarios — propose-safe at every autonomy dial setting (stated explicitly in the tool description and the returned `RuntimeImpact`).
- Wires both into `serve.go`'s outbox trace summarizer, and documents the chat phrasing next to the CLI command in `README.md` and the scaffolded `scenarios/README.md` (`cli/deployrepo.go`) — the dual-audience contract.

## Deviation note

Per the C9 spec's constraint ("do NOT touch mallcop-pro in this slice ... verify and note"): I verified (read-only) that mallcop-pro's console proxies investigate tools generically — `docs/chat-investigate-protocol.md`'s `tool_call`/`tool_result` trace carries a bare tool name + summary string with no console-side tool allowlist found in `internal/server`.
